key_insight: SCOPE guides quantum circuit compilation with a physics-based execution-time surrogate rather than gate count or depth alone.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing pulse execution latency can help fit quantum computations within limited coherence times.
method: Estimate nonlocal implementation time using operator Schmidt angular distance and a coupling-limited evolution-rate bound.
Combine trace-angle and waveform constraints with critical-path scoring to guide genetic search and mutation-region selection.
Use local quantum optimal control (QOC) to determine final pulse durations.
evidence_signal: Under a numerical nearest-neighbor control model, all 104 results across 13 instances beat adapted EPOC on QOC critical-path duration, with a 42.50% equally weighted reduction across eight-run instance means and a 2.00× geometric mean speedup.
watch_item: Results are numerical and control-model-specific; hardware performance and the computational cost of final QOC optimization require validation.
paper_title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
